A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching main sections and Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, references, and figures are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture regression and classification simulations, experiments using cGAN-generated Fashion-MNIST samples, and additional analyses in Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations and classification results in Section 6 and the appendices. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The two-layer architecture, single first-layer gradient update, separate-sample ridge fitting, and Hermite activation replacement remain unchanged (Equations 1–5 and 16–17). The mathematical corrections do not establish a different training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same Gaussian-mixture regression/classification scenarios and cGAN-generated Fashion-MNIST binary tasks: T-shirt/top versus Trouser and Sandal versus Ankle boot. The nonzero-component-mean experiments in Appendix F are also retained.

E2.justification: Both retain neural-network/Hermite-model comparisons for ReLU, tanh, and Sigmoid, plus the equivalent-linear-model comparison in Figure 4b. Both omit the Hermite comparator beyond beta = 1 in Figure 7b. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Equation 6 changes the training-error data term from half the sum of squared residuals to half their mean; Equation 7 adds a factor of 1/2 to generalization error. Appendix E changes the signal multiplier before adding noise from n/Tr(Sigma_1) to sqrt(n/Tr(Sigma_1)). These are limited revisions to reported specifications; experimental reruns are not established.

E4.justification: The sensitivity analyses of network width, alpha/beta, mixture ratio, component alignment, and covariance rank remain unchanged. Appendices D and F retain the same higher-learning-rate and nonzero-mean investigations, with no added or removed analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 20 Monte Carlo simulations for Figures 1, 2, and 4, including the same data-resampling statement for Figure 2. Repetition counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result plots, including those in the appendices, are identical across versions. The reported trends and model-equivalence findings are also unchanged. Revised metric and preprocessing descriptions are not accompanied by new or corrected numerical results.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects the gradient decomposition from A+B+C to A+B−C and the residual to B−C (Equations 19 and 32). Missing transposes are supplied in cross-covariance products, and Lemma 10's proof specifies a Frobenius norm. Alongside the error-normalization corrections, these are local mathematical repairs; theorem scope, assumptions, and proof strategies remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about conditional Gaussian and finite-degree Hermite equivalence under structured Gaussian mixtures, the role of data spread and learning rate, and empirical validation. No core contribution is added, removed, or strengthened.

C2.justification: The interpretations of data structure, mixture alignment/rank, and nonzero means remain the same, as do the limitations concerning the strength-parameter range. Section 6 rephrases the rank/eigenvalue explanation without changing its meaning; no substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Appendix E revises the explicit preprocessing instructions to use square-root rescaling and newly identifies the preprocessed sample in that formula. The cGAN hyperparameters, one-million-samples-per-class moment estimation, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to isotropic-input, spiked-covariance, and Gaussian-mixture research remain unchanged. Section 3 receives grammatical edits, while the reference list retains the same works.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered grammatical corrections, lightly rewrites the covariance-rank explanation, consolidates author/affiliation text, and expands the funding acknowledgments. Section order, appendix organization, and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author block is reformatted, with limited local equation/text reflow and caption wording edits in Figures 5 and 9. All nine figures retain the same visual content, panels, axes, and legends; there is no substantial display reorganization.

improvement.justification: v3 removes explicit mathematical inconsistencies: Equation 6 now matches the ridge objective in Equation 5, the gradient decomposition has the correct sign, and cross-covariance products and a proof norm are corrected. Preprocessing instructions and prose are also clearer. These provide a limited improvement in accuracy and documentation; the scientific claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and reruns under the revised specifications are not documented.
